_meta.indication: Natazia is an estrogen/progestin combination oral contraceptive (COC) indicated for use by women to prevent pregnancy; efficacy in women with BMI >30 kg/m2 has not been evaluated.

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, uncontrolled Phase 3 trial run for 20 cycles (28 days each)
pivotal_trials.population: Healthy women aged 18-50 (mean 30.3) in Europe at study sites in Germany (27), Austria (18) and Spain (5)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Pearl Index (number of pregnancies), the primary efficacy endpoint assessing contraceptive reliability
pivotal_trials.result: 9 pregnancies; unadjusted Pearl Index 1.04 (upper 95% CI 1.97) in women 18-35

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, uncontrolled Phase 3 trial run for 28 cycles (28 days each) in the US and Canada
pivotal_trials.population: Healthy women aged 18-35 (mean 24.0) in the US (20 sites) and Canada (9 sites)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Pearl Index (number of pregnancies), the primary efficacy endpoint for contraceptive reliability
pivotal_trials.result: 5 pregnancies; unadjusted Pearl Index 1.64 (upper 95% CI 3.82) in women 18-35

key_safety: Most common treatment-emergent adverse reactions (≥2%): headache including migraines (13.2%), metrorrhagia and irregular menstruation (8.0%), breast pain/discomfort/tenderness (6.6%), nausea or vomiting (6.5%), acne (3.9%) and increased weight (2.8%). Serious adverse reactions reported include deep vein thrombosis, myocardial infarction, focal nodular hyperplasia of the liver, uterine leiomyoma, and ruptured ovarian cyst.
target_moa: Combination oral contraceptive (estradiol valerate, a prodrug of 17β-estradiol, plus the progestin dienogest) that lowers the risk of pregnancy primarily by suppressing ovulation, with changes in cervical secretion and endometrium as additional mechanisms.
modality: Small molecule (combination of two steroid hormones: estradiol valerate and the progestin dienogest)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: CIGARETTE SMOKING AND SERIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR EVENTS — Cigarette smoking increases the risk of serious cardiovascular events from COC use; this risk increases with age, particularly in women over 35, so COCs should not be used by women over 35 who smoke.

advisory_committee.vote: Not presented to an advisory committee because the clinical study design was acceptable and the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues; DRUP did not believe AC guidance was needed to decide approvability for prevention of pregnancy.

description.text: Added safety labeling on VTE risk temporal trend when starting/restarting a COC (no new indication)

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for the inclusion of new information regarding the risk of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in women using combined oral contraceptives (COCs) in WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS, subsection Thromboembolic Disorders and Other Vascular Problems. The new information specifically concerns the temporal trend in the increased risk relative to starting a COC or restarting the same or a different COC following temporary discontinuation. summary.text: Natazia (estradiol valerate/dienogest) was approved under a standard NDA (505(b)) for prevention of pregnancy, supported by two pivotal open-label contraceptive trials demonstrating acceptable Pearl Indexes; the application was not referred to an advisory committee, and a 505(o) postmarketing requirement (expanded INAS-EV cohort safety study of thrombotic risk) was imposed.

citations.quote: Approval is recommended for the Applicant's proposed primary indication for EV/DNG, that of "Prevention of pregnancy in women of reproductive age."

Please refer to your July 2, 2009 New Drug Application (NDA), received July 6, 2009, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Natazia (estradiol valerate and estradiol valerate/dienogest) Tablets.
Therefore, based on appropriate scientific data, FDA has determined that you are required to conduct the following:

requirement.text: PMR 1637-1: A prospective, controlled, non-interventional, long-term cohort study of new users of Natazia and new users of oral contraceptives containing other progestins, expanding the ongoing European INAS-EV surveillance study to include US women, enrolling at least 50,000 women in the US and Europe followed for at least three years to assess thrombotic risks (DVT, PE, acute MI, cerebrovascular accidents).

citations.quote: 1637-1. A prospective, controlled, non-interventional, long-term cohort study that follows a series of cohorts consisting of new users of Natazia (estradiol valerate and estradiol valerate/dienogest) tablets and new users of oral contraceptives containing other progestins.
The expanded study should enroll a total of at least 50,000 women in the US and Europe, who will be followed for at least three years.
The main clinical outcomes of interest are deep venous thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolus (PE), acute myocardial infarction, and cerebrovascular accidents.
